review.note: Drafted by the assistant in M44b under the owner's dated exception, from the sources named and not from a reading of them; the argument is the thing to check, not only the dates.

explanation: The second war was fought over the spoils of the first. The Balkan League had agreed how to divide Ottoman Europe before it went to war, and it could not hold to that agreement once it had won. The powers denied Serbia the Adriatic coast, so Serbia wanted compensation in the Macedonian districts promised to Bulgaria. Greece had taken Salonika. Bulgaria attacked its allies on 29 June 1913 instead of accepting arbitration. The claim is the ordinary one and it is narrow. The first war made the quarrel the second was about, and it did not make the second inevitable.
